description: RRT* grows a tree like RRT, but it also improves the tree as it grows. A new node takes the parent that gives it the cheapest path among its neighbours, not only the nearest node. Then each neighbour that is cheaper to reach through the new node moves under it (*rewiring*). With enough samples, the best path converges to an optimal one (*asymptotic optimality*). The neighbourhood shrinks as the tree grows, as `γ (ln n / n)^(1/d)`. In `sampling-planning` it can minimize another cost objective than path length, such as a risk along the path, while neighbours are still found by distance; the guarantee of asymptotic optimality holds for metric costs like path length, not for every objective. With the `parallel` feature, `grow_forest` grows one tree per thread from its own random stream and then merges the trees into the first one: every merged node is connected like a new RRT* node and rewires its neighbours, so the best path is never worse than the first tree's, and the result does not depend on thread scheduling.

papers.title: Sampling-based algorithms for optimal motion planning
